decisions.reason: Product A is close to the firm's established software and regulatory workflow knowledge, allowing the firm to assimilate user feedback and continue improving it, so discontinuation is unlikely.
Product B builds on the firm's existing training content and customer support capabilities, giving it the absorptive capacity to interpret demand and adjust the offer, so it is likely kept.
Product C is based on the firm's customer support and software engineering expertise, enabling it to learn from usage data and improve the tool, so it is likely kept.
Product D leverages the firm's existing practice management data and software engineering knowledge, so the firm can recognize its value and refine it, making dropping improbable.
Product E is a bundle of closely related existing offerings, well within the firm's established knowledge, so the firm can manage and improve it with low uncertainty, making discontinuation unlikely.
Product F is distant from the firm's core practice management knowledge, limiting its ability to interpret performance feedback and apply improvements, so it is a strong candidate for dropping.
